body.x: The Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that it successfully operated the “Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion” at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), showcasing IFEZ’s future city vision and innovative Incheon-based companies on the global stage.

Under the theme “Destination Incheon – From Smart City to AI City,” the Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion was designed to present a sustainable urban future realized through the technologies of Incheon’s innovation-driven companies.

During CES 2026, the pavilion attracted approximately 15,000 visitors, underscoring strong global interest in Incheon’s innovation ecosystem and future city vision and bringing the exhibition to a successful close.

In addition, the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority held meetings with the Fairfax County Economic Development Authority (FCEDA) during the event. The two sides exchanged views on support measures and cooperation models to facilitate the entry of Incheon startups into the U.S. market and agreed to gradually develop practical joint programs to support the global expansion of Incheon-based companies.

Incheon’s innovative companies also delivered notable results. The authority supported the participation of 50 companies at CES 2026, including 10 startups in the Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion, 10 companies in the KOTRA Pavilion at Eureka Park, 6 companies in the Global Pavilion, 15 companies in the visiting delegation, and 9 companies in the Innovation Awards Showcase.

body.cap: Officials from the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority meet with the Fairfax County Economic Development Authority (FCEDA) to discuss support measures and cooperation models for Incheon startups’ entry into the U.S. market during CES 2026 | Image by Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority

body.x: These companies conducted a total of 1,419 export consultations with overseas buyers and investors during the exhibition—an increase of more than 400 cases compared to the previous year—with the total consultation value reaching approximately USD 560 million. Among them, nine companies successfully signed 20 memoranda of understanding (MOUs), expanding opportunities for global market entry and domestic investment attraction.

Leadpoint System, a smart manufacturing and industrial automation solutions provider, signed an MOU with U.S.-based technology R&D firm Webtronic Labs. Fire detection and safety management solutions provider EMCITY concluded an MOU with Texas Legacy Realty to apply fire safety and safe-zone solutions to commercial and residential buildings in Texas.
In the regenerative medicine and bio-healthcare sector, Medicell Healthcare signed an MOU with the City of Phoenix to explore cooperation on public healthcare technology and local pilot projects.

Moreover, 14 companies supported by the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority received 17 CES 2026 Innovation Awards, the highest number ever. The award-winning companies drew strong interest from global buyers and investors, further highlighting the technological competitiveness of Incheon startups.

In particular, Deep Fusion AI, a company specializing in radar-based sensor fusion AI technology, was selected as a CES 2026 Best of Innovation Award honoree, earning high praise as a leading player in next-generation autonomous driving and robotic perception technologies.

Incheon Mayor Jeong-bok Yoo stated, “Through our participation in CES, we have presented the AI City vision of Incheon–IFEZ on the global stage and taken another step closer to realizing ‘Global Top 10 City Incheon.’ We will continue to actively support Incheon companies’ global expansion and develop Incheon into a global business hub.”
